author: James Joyce
title: Dubliners
edition: New York: B. W. Huebsch, second printing, April 1917 (US first printing December 1916); scan-backed Wikisource transcription of 1917 Dubliners by James Joyce.djvu. HTML emphasis becomes plain text; page-number markers and zero-width page-boundary characters removed, prose line wrapping folded to spaces; original paragraph and embedded verse boundaries retained. The printed row of spaced full stops marking the section break in Eveline (p. 47) is reproduced as its own line of nine spaced periods. The library text holds all fifteen stories in the book's order, each under its printed title; the title page and contents are omitted. On 2026-11-18 Counterparts after its section break, A Mother and Grace were collated word by word against the OCR of Internet Archive dubliners00joycuoft (the scan the Wikisource file was made from) and, to catch misreadings the transcription shares with that OCR, against Project Gutenberg’s Dubliners (ebook 2814), every difference decided on the item’s page images: three readings were corrected (A Mother “Mansion House. He”, Grace “constable, Jack,” and “Mr. Kernan” for “Keman”), and the section breaks in Counterparts (p. 113) and Grace (pp. 197, 219), which the transcription gives as six asterisks, are written as the printed rows of eight spaced full stops. The transcription joined some printed paragraphs and left out most of p. 169, the first eight stanzas and two lines of Hynes’s poem in Ivy Day in the Committee Room; the fidelity pass below restored both. A fidelity pass on 2026-11-18 compared the whole text with Project Gutenberg’s ebook 2814 word by word and for punctuation and with the hOCR line indents of IA dubliners00joycuoft, and decided every difference on that item’s page images. Twelve further readings were corrected: “wash him” (The Sisters), “nearest. I hid” (An Encounter), “won. Farley” (After the Race), “I say, Tommy,” and “Hushed are the winds” (A Little Cloud), “honour. Farrington” (Counterparts), “O, I know all about it!” (Clay), “O’Connor. “Anyway”, “Hynes. “Tricky”, “trouble you, Jack,” and “stout, Jack,” (Ivy Day) and “Cunningham, “Jack” (Grace). The section breaks at blocks 322, 436, 1311 and 1483, which the transcription gave as six asterisks, are the printed rows of eight spaced full stops. In Hynes’s poem the last three stanzas read “Phœnix”, “flames,” and “day,” as printed, and the even lines of every stanza are indented two spaces as printed; the other verse in the book keeps the transcription’s unindented lines. Slips of the print itself are kept: “o’cock” and “dignity’ sake” (A Painful Case), “his. footsteps” (A Little Cloud), the closing quotation mark after “that was why.” (The Dead). The fidelity pass then restored p. 169 from its page image: the eight stanzas (blocks 833-840) and the two lines that open the next stanza, so that the whole poem reads as printed. It also restored the 22 printed paragraph breaks that the transcription joins, each found by the hOCR indents and by Project Gutenberg’s paragraphing and confirmed on the page image: three in The Sisters, two in The Boarding House, six in Ivy Day, three in A Mother and eight in Grace. Two printed paragraphs that the transcription divided in two were joined on 2026-11-18, with every later citation renumbered: in A Little Cloud (“Yes, that’s agreed,” … “Next year if I come, parole d’honneur.”) and in Grace (“We’ll make a new man of him,” … “Good-night, Mrs. Kernan.”). The cards in The Sisters and Ivy Day, printed as centred and hanging lines, stay separate paragraphs.

rights.basis: The English text in this 1917 edition was published before 1931; its US publication copyright term has expired as of 2026. The linked primary transcription/catalogue identifies its US public-domain status. No later editorial introduction is included.

acquisition.method: Wikisource MediaWiki parse API (action=parse, prop=text), one request per story subpage in printed order: The Sisters, An Encounter, Araby, Eveline, After the Race, Two Gallants, The Boarding House, A Little Cloud, Counterparts, Clay, A Painful Case, Ivy Day in the Committee Room, A Mother, Grace, The Dead (main-namespace revisions 14966105, 5179127, 6617246, 5179133, 5179150, 5179157, 5917680, 10774318, 5930415, 10774329, 9933978, 5930417, 10774324, 6587783, 14966104). downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the fifteen JSON responses concatenated in that order; downloadUrl is the first of them. Only the transcluded scan text (div.prp-pages-output) is used: Wikisource headers, notes, audio links, page-number anchors and zero-width page-boundary characters removed; HTML emphasis dropped to plain text; whitespace collapsed to single spaces; HTML line breaks kept as stanza lines, blank lines between verse lines splitting stanzas; each story's centred title became a heading; the Eveline section-break row of dots is written as nine spaced full stops, as the edition note states. On 2026-11-18 blocks 502, 973 and 1201 (six asterisks) became the printed row of eight spaced full stops and blocks 872, 1014 and 1137 were corrected, each on the page images of IA dubliners00joycuoft; paragraph boundaries in those passages were compared with the line indents in that item’s hOCR. The other asterisk lines (blocks 322, 436, 1311, 1483) became the same printed rows in the fidelity pass of 2026-11-18, which also corrected blocks 45, 86, 203, 380, 444, 511, 563, 661, 683, 761, 780, 822-824 and 1055 on the page images after a word and punctuation comparison with Project Gutenberg ebook 2814 (pg2814.txt), and set Hynes’s poem with its printed indents. The renumbering of the fidelity pass then inserted the eight stanzas of p. 169 before the stanza beginning “No sound of strife” and split 21 blocks at the 22 restored paragraph openings (node tools/reading-library.js remap, which re-cited every school night and calendar reading); block numbers earlier in this record refer to the text before it, which had 1672 blocks.
